key_insight: EEG-Xplain provides a unified attribution framework to make black-box EEG foundation models interpretable across spatial, temporal, and frequency dimensions.
engineering_relevance: It gives practitioners a standardized way to validate EEG model reliability, physiological plausibility, and clinical trust before deployment.
method: Combines gradient-, perturbation-, and activation-based explainers across heterogeneous EEG architectures.
Maps important channels, time segments, and rhythms using topographic, heatmap, and spectral perturbation analyses.
Uses AOPC and cross-method consistency to score explanation reliability, then converts outputs into LLM-generated natural-language reports.
evidence_signal: Experiments on Mumtaz2016 and TUAB show explanations aligned with known neurophysiological markers while also revealing artifact and spurious-pattern dependencies.
watch_item: Interpretability results can still be influenced by artifacts and explanation-method disagreement, so reliability checks are essential.
paper_title: EEG-Xplain: Decoding Neural Black-Boxes of EEG Foundation Models
